title: IBLA 2022-111 ) Special Use Permit #220029 (IBLA 2022-111)
text:
March 9, 2022
IBLA 2022-111 ) Special Use Permit #220029
)
ATLANTIC TIDE AND TURNOUT, LLC ) Special Use Permit
)
) Appeal Dismissed
ORDER
This Board received a notice of appeal from Atlantic Tide and Turnout, LLC
(Atlantic Tide)1 and docketed the appeal as IBLA 2022-111. The notice of appeal
involves a special use permit (SUP) issued by the Superintendent, Cape Cod National
Seashore, National Park Service (NPS).2 Subsequently, we received from Atlantic Tide a
statement of reasons and a petition for stay, among other documents.3
However, our jurisdiction is limited to adjudicating appeals of “decisions rendered
by Departmental officials relating to” public lands and their resources, mineral resources
in acquired and offshore lands, and surface coal mining.4 Because of our limited
jurisdiction, we may only adjudicate appeals of decisions rendered by a “Bureau or
Office” or an administrative law judge within the Office of Hearings and Appeals.5 As
reflected in our regulations, “Bureau or Office” means the Bureau of Indian Affairs, the
Bureau of Land Management, the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement
(BSEE), the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM), the Office of Natural
Resources Revenue, the Deputy Assistant Secretary – Natural Resources Revenue, “or any
1 Notice of Appeal of Cape Cod National Seashore Special Use Permit # 220029 (filed
Mar. 7, 2022).
2 Id. at 1; id., Attached Special Use Permit (dated Feb. 18, 2022).
3 See Letter of Appeal from Atlantic Tide (filed Mar. 9, 2022).
4 43 C.F.R. § 4.1(b)(2) (2020); see also 43 U.S.C. § 1702(e) (2018) (defining “public
lands” as lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management).
5 43 C.F.R. §§ 4.410(a), 4.400 (2020).

IBLA 2022-111
successor organization, as appropriate.”6 As the lands at issue are not “public lands”7 and
NPS is not listed as a “Bureau or Office” whose decision we may review, we have no
authority to adjudicate NPS’s decision to issue the SUP. Accordingly, we dismiss IBLA
2022-111 for lack of jurisdiction.8
________________________________ I concur: ____________________________________
Steven J. Lechner Silvia Riechel Idziorek
Acting Chief Administrative Judge Acting Deputy Chief Administrative Judge
6 Id. § 4.400. BSEE and BOEM are successors of the Bureau of Ocean Energy
Management, Regulation and Enforcement. See Black Elk Energy Offshore Operations,
LLC, 182 IBLA 331, 332 n.2 (2012).
7 See 54 U.S.C. 100501 (2018) (defining the National Park System as those lands and
waters managed by the Director, NPS).
8 See WildLands Defense, 192 IBLA 209, 214 (2018) (explaining that if the requirements
of 43 C.F.R. § 4.410 are not met, the appeal must be dismissed for lack of jurisdiction);
see also 36 C.F.R. Parts 1-79 (2021) (indicating that NPS regulations do not provide for
any appeals to this Board); id. §§ 8.6, 9.14, 20.4 (indicating that certain NPS appeals
may be heard by other units within the Office of Hearings and Appeals).
